---
title: "Program"
---

## Introduction

Process modelling, identification and control. The ideal infinite-horizon constrained optimal control problem as the common thread of the course.

## Part 1. Process control with Model Predictive Control [MPC]{.part .part-mpc}

- MPC formulation: stage cost, terminal cost, model, state and input constraints, terminal constraints.
- Infinite-horizon constrained control; unconstrained LQR and the Riccati equation; dual-mode control.
- Main properties of MPC: optimality, recursive feasibility, stability (Lyapunov theory).
- Value function interpretation of MPC and explicit MPC.
- Economic MPC.
- MPC with mixed-integer variables and logical-dynamical constraints (MLD systems).
- Applications: smart charging of electric vehicles, building energy management, task scheduling in assembly lines, traffic control.
- Beyond the nominal case: unmeasured states and offset-free MPC; robust and stochastic MPC (overview).
- Implementation of MPC algorithms in Julia (JuMP).

## Part 2. Process control with Reinforcement Learning [RL]{.part .part-rl}

- From MPC to dynamic programming: Bellman's principle.
- The RL setting: Markov decision processes, policies, returns, value functions.
- Bellman equations and Bellman optimality equations.
- Dynamic programming: policy evaluation, policy iteration, value iteration.
- Monte Carlo and temporal-difference methods; SARSA and Q-learning.
- Function approximation and deep RL (DDPG, overview of policy-gradient methods).
- Hybrid MPC–RL algorithms and similarities between MPC and RL.

## Part 3. Process identification and state estimation [ID]{.part .part-id}

::: {.callout-note}
The identification part of the program may be subject to changes.
:::

- Problem definition: white-, grey- and black-box models; the identification loop.
- Statistical estimators and their properties; Cramér–Rao bound.
- Linear and weighted least squares; regularization; maximum likelihood and Bayesian (MAP) estimation; nonlinear least squares.
- Recursive least squares and forgetting.
- Dynamic models: ARX, output error, ARMAX, Box–Jenkins; one-step and multi-step predictors; prediction error methods.
- Experiment design (persistency of excitation, PRBS and multisine inputs) and model validation (residual analysis, cross-validation, order selection).
- State estimation: Kalman filter, extended Kalman filter, moving horizon estimation as the dual of MPC.
- Data-driven predictive control: Willems' fundamental lemma and DeePC.
- Time series for forecasting exogenous inputs; overview of advanced methods (grey-box ODE models, learning-based MPC).
- Implementation examples in Julia and Python.
